_notes.scope: Development-only pilot training harness on ONE video / ONE scene. All losses and metrics on these windows are in-sample. No independent split exists, so none is created.
_notes.hyperparameters: A-priori engineering defaults for a smoke-scale run (20 epochs, cosine decay to 1% of the peak rate, clipping at 10). Learning rate 0.003 was preferred over 0.001 in a single two-value, 2-epoch engineering probe that looked only at in-sample training loss (and that gradients flow); no other search or tuning was performed and nothing was tuned for accuracy. The decoder predicts raw pixel offsets (P5.6 contract), which is why a moderately high peak learning rate is used.
_notes.checkpoint_selection: FINAL_EPOCH_ONLY: periodic checkpoints (every checkpoint_every_epochs and the last epoch) are for resumption and inspection; no best-checkpoint selection on correlated windows of the same video.
_notes.weight_decay: applied to weight matrices (ndim >= 2) only; biases and normalisation parameters are not decayed.
_notes.seed: controls the window order of each epoch (default_rng([seed, epoch])) and torch global RNG; model initialisation uses the encoder init_seed and decoder_seed.
_notes.device: cpu | cuda | auto; 'cuda' fails explicitly when no device exists.
_notes.torch_threads: 1 for bitwise reproducibility on CPU: with several threads some backward reductions are not bitwise reproducible (measured: forward identical, gradients of 12 parameter tensors differed between identical runs); with 1 thread two runs, and a resumed run, produce byte-identical checkpoints. Costs wall-clock time (about 1.3 s per batch of 64 windows). null = PyTorch default.
